newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Michelin, Bridgestone buy rubber in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Michelin, Bridgestone buy rubber in Singapore.

text.p: Michelin and Bridgestone were said to have bought several hundred tonnes of rubber in modest trade on Tuesday in the Singapore rubber exchange and may pick up more material in the coming days, dealers said.

"Michelin is still buying RSS3 while Bridgestone bought some TSR20 rubber. I suppose you can call it bargain-hunting since prices look fairly attractive to them," a dealer said. There were no immediate details on the price of the purchases.
Michelin picked up RSS3 rubber for the second day running while some of the purchases by Bridgestone were said to have been concluded late on Monday, the dealers said.
Goodyear was said to have asked for quotes in the market but there were no reports that it managed to conclude a deal.

Except for the buying by the two companies, trading was quiet with most of the rubber business watching out for any sign that the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) may intervene in the market.

At around 0945 GMT, September RSS3 was seen steady at 94.25 U.S. cents a kg. October TSR20 was seen unchanged at 101.00 U.S. cents a kg. September RSS1 was seen flat at 138.50 Singapore cents (96 U.S. cents) a kg.
